title: Essay: what happened when the place became somebody's job (the sequel to Tasks are tasks), for a fresh reader
description:
## The piece

An **essay** for the Library (`docs/papers/harbour/`, `kind: essay`, under `docs/papers/standard.md`), for **a fresh human reader**: someone who has never seen Harbour, the Survey or the loop. It is the sequel to *Tasks are tasks, and the codebase is a place* (`docs/papers/harbour/tasks-are-tasks.md`, v5).

That essay diagnosed a problem: nobody's job is the place. It ended by asking for a forecast before each task, for the builders to be asked why the work was difficult, and for the result to be scored. This essay tells what happened when a loop made the place somebody's job for three days, and what that showed.

The technical record is the paper *Can a task finish with the codebase cleaner than it started?* (`docs/papers/harbour/cleaner-than-it-started.md`, LIN-4315). The essay draws on it and cites it. It does not carry the paper's evidence; it argues, narrates and shows.

## The argument, roughly (the writer may sharpen or change it)

When the loop **finishes a move**, the area of code ends cleaner. "Finishing" means the planned work merged and the copies the change left behind were gathered straight after. The effect is small but real, and reading it differently doesn't make it go away. Ordinary tickets, one at a time, are not shown to make things better or worse.

What makes the difference is **finishing**: deleting the copies, not adding a new owner beside them. And the human's job turns out to be the size of the move, and holding the authority, more than the detail of the work.

## Material (all at commits on main; check each against its source)

* **The diagnosis and its images,** from *Tasks are tasks*: the contractor and the resident; the ball (where a change binds); the drill and the chisel; John's forcefield; the trig point.
* **The loop as it came to run** (`docs/plans/survey/notes-2026-11-05.md`, "The loop, as it runs now"):
  * a Survey before the work;
  * the person's scope call;
  * a tidy first, where the change binds;
  * blind, code-only reads at merge;
  * the builder's after-answers;
  * a tidy-after of the copies left at the edges, with a stop rule.
* **How the first measure was overturned:** the operator's own ledger rated the work much better, then blind readers rated it level. Honesty about that is part of the story (the paper; `place-ledger.md`).
* **The results, sized honestly.** The paper's findings, and **two pieces of evidence that came after its freeze:**
  * **the baseline.** Ordinary pre-loop pairs of changes, read the same way, came out better in both passes on 1 of 4, against 7 of 7 for the loop's finished areas. The one baseline pair that read better was itself a consolidation. See `docs/plans/survey/place-ledger.md`, "Next 2: a baseline for the area reads", and `log.md`, 6 Nov 12:30 and 13:10.
  * **independent readings after the paper's window:** Seams & Tangles run 9 (`docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-2026-11-06-run9.md`), no area worse; Drift & Coherence run 5 (`docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-06.md`), "better, small", with one area mixed.
* **What the tidier code actually looks like** (concrete, from the code):
  * hand-written test fakes 56 → 6 in two days, the 6 left being honest stops;
  * about 50 dead method-presence guards deleted under a check that stops them coming back;
  * an authority decision (the periodical grant) made in two places, now one rule;
  * a silent 50-comment cap found by the paper and fixed (it was hiding review comments from the close-out gate).
* **Towers of Hanoi** (John, 5 Nov, in `log.md`): to move a feature cleanly you first move its tidy, and to move the tidy you first move its copies. A partial move held in place by a ratchet, then finished, is what turned the browser-test area around.
* **The human's role, and the turn** (`log.md`, `notes-2026-11-05.md`, the paper's Finding 9):
  * many of the copies the loop later cleaned up were *invited by the human's own instructions*: a byte-identical rule, a count rule, a sweep drawn by method name, a scope description that became a false comment;
  * John's reading, recorded in `log.md`, 6 Nov \~09:30: mistakes are expected when a hand holds the reins, and that is the case for moving those judgement points into Harbour as structure. The human calls stay human: the size of the move, the rulings, and granting authority. On 6 Nov John granted a new authority explicitly, as a human call.
* **Patterns** (`log.md`):
  * a sweep starts by writing its check;
  * a list or count kept by hand goes stale, while one derived from the code doesn't;
  * production code bent to fit a test fake, where the fake should have been fixed.
* **Cost, briefly:** the paper's figures. A tidy-after cost about half to most of its parent's bill. John's position: measure the premium for now, don't optimise it yet.

## Visual storytelling

The Library serves SVG and PNG figures, referenced inline as `![alt](figures/<slug>/<name>.svg)`, with files under `docs/papers/harbour/figures/<slug>/` (see `browser-flakes.md`, `cheaper-capacity.md`). Two to four figures that carry the story, for example:

* the loop, before / during / after, as one diagram;
* the areas moving from "mixed" to "better", beside the baseline pairs that stayed mixed;
* the census falling from 56 to 6 over two days, merge by merge (the paper's `git/census-by-merge.json` and the merges after it);
* the ball, with copies at the edges where a change binds.

Every figure is generated from data at a commit, with its script beside it, and labelled so a fresh reader can follow it without the text. No figure claims more than its data.

## Tone and balance

* **Narrative and big-picture,** for someone new: define every term on first use, or avoid it. The paper's formality is not the model here.
* **Neither oversell nor undersell (John):** the direction is real and small; state it as plainly as its limits. Lead with what happened and what changed in the code, not with what wasn't shown.
* **Mark John's words and images as his,** as *Tasks are tasks* does. A model's readings are marked as that.
* **No status claims that will go stale.** Write what was true at the commit you cite.

## Done when

* The essay is at `docs/papers/harbour/<a name the writer chooses>.md`, with `kind: essay` and the Library header (`argument`, `sources` at commits). Its figures and their scripts sit beside it.
* An index row is added in `docs/papers/README.md` (two sentences at most).
* **Two fresh readers before merge,** each given only the file:
  * one new to Harbour, the main audience: does the story land, and is anything unexplained?
  * one for accuracy against the paper and the sources.

  Fix what they find, and say what was fixed.
* It merges through the usual review.

## Report back

The essay's argument in two sentences, what the fresh readers changed, and anything the record couldn't support.

**Sequence (6 Nov):** this essay runs after LIN-4331 (the paper's v2) merges, and cites v2 for every number.

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

Both Surveys (on this ticket, 12:33–12:34 comment time) found the essay's newest evidence was then off main. That is settled now: the notebook was synced (LIN-4332, `1c894016`), and **the paper's version 2 has merged** (LIN-4331 / LIN-4334, `ea352306`; `docs/papers/harbour/cleaner-than-it-started.md`, `version: 2`, grounded at `509f797e`). The person's scope call:

1. **Every number comes from version 2,** cited to it, or to its evidence folder `cleaner-than-it-started-evidence/2026-11-06-v2/`. The essay introduces no number of its own. In particular, use v2's unit and wording:
   * "**nine area readings over fifteen tickets, all better in both passes, and no pass read one worse**", not the notebook's "seven areas";
   * the **pair baseline** as v2 states it: one of four ordinary pairs read better in both passes, and that pair was a consolidation. So reading a pair as one area doesn't by itself make it read better. It is not loop against no loop, and the circularity stands. The fair line for the essay is "*what reads better is consolidation, and the loop's finished moves are consolidations*".
2. **The census as its own definition.** 56 → 6 counts hand-written fake DOMs on the census's list, all six left being stops. v2 Finding 6 and Drift run 5 say a cruder count of `makeContainer|createElement` *rose* 46 → 51. Telling that honestly is the essay's tone at its best. Drift run 5's one mixed area, "production code shaped for tests", is the essay's own pattern; use it.
3. **Facts after both Periodical windows are facts, not Periodical verdicts.** The census reaching 6 (LIN-4312) and the comment fix (LIN-4322; `GET /issues/LIN-4150` returned all 143 comments after deploy) can be stated as what happened. Don't say a Periodical judged them better: v2's Limits and Next 3 say no Periodical has read those merges.
4. **Figures:**
   * the script lives in `<slug>-scripts/` (as `theseus-method-scripts/` does);
   * it reads version 2's evidence folder in place, and doesn't re-derive data into a second copy;
   * the files go under `figures/<slug>/`.
   * Every figure is generated, labelled for a reader who skips the text, and claims nothing beyond v2.
5. **Cite** `path@sha:line` **and comment or git times,** never the notebook's clock headings (they drift up to about 1.5 h on 6 Nov, as v2 says).
6. **Registries:** a README row of two sentences, with no version history. `proposals.md` was already dispositioned by v2; leave it, unless the essay itself adds a line, and then say why.

The tone, balance and fresh-reader steps in the description stand. Lead with what happened and what changed in the code; size it as v2 does; mark John's words and images as his.

---

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned at close-out. The full plan (drift corrections, the seven decisions, the break/witness table, landing order) is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.*

**Implemented:** the essay `docs/papers/harbour/the-place-became-somebodys-job.md`, three generated figures with `the-place-became-somebodys-job-scripts/charts.mjs`, one README row, one `proposals.md` line, and the library essay-count pin (13 to 14), in PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2340](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2340>), merged as `b76d5239`. The plan was implemented as approved, with these deviations: the close-out fixed the blind-read prompt citation (`@ea352306`) and Figure 1's layout (arrows, clipped text, label), which the rendered-page check found.

Session fit: fits one session

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4330 @ afe9074fd

Read at `afe9074f` (origin/main, 6 Nov 12:09Z) in a scratch worktree. The essay itself isn't hard. Writing it is mostly judgement about tone. What's hard is the evidence: the newest and strongest material isn't on main yet, and the figures have to be redrawn from moving data.

**1. Half the "after the freeze" material isn't on main.** The notebook was last synced at `1d10f9b3` (LIN-4314, to branch `98670be3b`). On main, `docs/plans/survey/log.md` ends at **6 Nov 08:15**. None of these appear at BASE:
- John's "hand holds the reins" reading (6 Nov ~09:30; the only 09:30 entry is 5 Nov's second blind pass);
- the 12:30 / 13:10 baseline entries (log 12:30 is 5 Nov's LIN-4246; there's no 13:10);
- `place-ledger.md` "Next 2: a baseline for the area reads".

The 1-of-4 vs 7-of-7 baseline carries the most weight of anything in the brief, because it answers the paper's own Limit ("nothing outside the loop was scored per area the same way"). Right now it can't be cited at a commit on main. Of the brief's sources, these are on main: both Periodicals (`fa3bd87a`, `b9fc60ab`), the census at 6 (all `// stop:`), the guards ratchet, the grant rule (`f2816e17`) and the comment fix (`badec1fb`).

**2. The counts don't line up.** The paper says "six area readings covering eleven tickets" and "twelve subjects better in both". The brief says "7 of 7 finished areas". The essay has to say what an "area" is and how six became seven. Otherwise the accuracy reader will catch the mismatch, or a fresh reader will be misled. The baseline is also newer than the paper and hasn't had a second check. The standard allows that for an essay, but only if the essay says so.

**3. The independent readings are less tidy than the brief makes them sound.** Drift run 5's "mixed" area is *production code shaped for tests*: `public/live-console.js` gained a second export surface for tests (LIN-4309/4310). That's the same move the essay will showcase, and it's an example of one of the brief's own three patterns. The same report counts a crude `makeContainer|createElement` grep that *rose* from 46 to 51. So "56 → 6" has to be described as the census's definition of a hand-written fake, not as "the fakes are gone". Paper Finding 6 already says the count is a proxy. If the essay loses that, it oversells. If it handles the point honestly, it's the best example of the essay's tone.

**4. The figures need data past the freeze.** `census-by-merge.json` stops at 18 (`1d10f9b3`). Getting to 6 means rerunning `census-by-merge.mjs` over `3f4d4131..afe9074f` at one cited commit. The standard says a figure in an essay "is read at its source". So the areas-vs-baseline figure also depends on point 1.

**5. Things that will go stale.** LIN-4254 was still landing at BASE (`afe9074f` is one of its pieces). Pin every number to a sha.

**Is this a symptom?** Partly. The notebook lives off main and gets synced by hand, ticket by ticket. That is the brief's own pattern: "a list kept by hand goes stale". This is the second write-up to depend on a sync.

**What I'd do first:** a LIN-4314-style notebook sync to main, notebook paths only, *before* drafting. Then pin one commit for everything the essay cites. Then extend the census series and recount "areas" to a single definition. Do all of that before writing any prose or figures.

## Survey global: LIN-4330 @ afe9074fd

**Where it lands.** `docs/papers/harbour/`, one of 13 essays. It sits next to its prequel `tasks-are-tasks.md` (v5) and its source paper `cleaner-than-it-started.md`. The figures go under `figures/<slug>/`, and there's a row in `docs/papers/README.md`. The Library finds documents by front-matter `kind` and serves only `.svg`/`.png` from `figures/` (`lib/library.js:368-534`), so nothing needs registering. The README index is the one hand-kept list. Nothing checks it, and nothing would notice a missing row. Its essay rows have grown to 685–2,163 characters each, carrying bylines and version history, well past the ticket's "two sentences".

**The deeper issue: the essay's newest sources aren't on main.** At this commit, `docs/plans/survey/log.md` ends at "08:00 UTC, 6 Nov" (the 08:15 filing of LIN-4314/4315). There is no ~09:30 entry with John's reins reading, no authority grant, and no 12:30 or 13:10 baseline entries. `place-ledger.md` ends at "four of four (5 Nov, 21:20)" and has no "Next 2: a baseline". `proposals.md:665` still asks the baseline question as open. A search for "12:30 UTC" in `log.md` finds 5 Nov's LIN-4246 entry. Log headings repeat clock times across days. Done the obvious way, the essay would cite a branch sha, or wait for a second hand sync like LIN-4314. Either way, its headline evidence rests on the off-main notebook problem the paper's Next 7 names. The two cited reviews are on main.

**What the obvious path adds.**
- **A fourth home for figure code.** Today it lives in three places: `scripts/survey-*-figures.mjs` (19 files, each with its own hand-rolled `esc`/`text` SVG helpers), `<slug>-scripts/` (`theseus-method-scripts/charts.mjs`, `coherence-as-it-grows-scripts/figure.py`), and the paper's `cleaner-than-it-started-scripts/`. A script inside `figures/<slug>/` would be ignored by the server but would add one more convention.
- **A second copy of the paper's data.** The census figure (56 → 6) needs merges after the paper's freeze. `census-by-merge.json` stops at `1d10f9b3`. The test at this commit lists 6 entries, all stops. If the extended series is re-derived into a new data file, the evidence ends up in two places.
- **A `proposals.md` line (Next).** If the essay reports the baseline as done, the open line at `:665` needs settling.

**What would leave it better, at a cost this task can carry.**
1. Sync the notebook to main before writing, and cite `path@sha:line`, never clock times.
2. Put the figure script in `<slug>-scripts/`, following theseus-method. Have it read the paper's evidence folder in place. Extend the census by running `cleaner-than-it-started-scripts/census-by-merge.mjs` into a new dated folder under the paper's evidence, so the paper's tool stays the only owner.
3. Keep the README row to two sentences: argument plus status, no version history.
4. Settle `proposals.md:665` rather than add a new line beside it.

**Better still, but not this task's job.** A shared SVG helper for the figure scripts. An index derived from the catalog, or a check that the README matches it (the essay's own pattern: "a list kept by hand goes stale"). And a home on main for live experiment records, so essays don't depend on hand syncs.

## LIN-4330: PR open, CI green

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2340 (branch `feat/lin-4330-place-became-somebodys-job`, commit `64e803df`, not merged; merge is for review).

- Essay: `docs/papers/harbour/the-place-became-somebodys-job.md` (kind: essay), every number from paper v2 (`cleaner-than-it-started.md`) and its evidence folder.
- Three figures, generated by `the-place-became-somebodys-job-scripts/charts.mjs` from the v2 evidence folder in place; `figure-theme --check` passes.
- README row (two sentences) and one `proposals.md` line for the essay's Next.
- Library test pin: essay count 13 to 14 (`tests/unit/library.test.js`).
- Two fresh readers (clarity; accuracy against v2 and cited commits). Their findings are fixed in the PR, including one wrong caption and one sentence that went beyond the paper.
- Checks: `npm run test:unit` 23,947 pass, 0 fail; CI (Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan, CI success) all SUCCESS.

Limits, stated in the essay: no Periodical has read LIN-4312, LIN-4322 or `afe9074f`; the untouched-area baseline is still open.

## Review — LIN-4330

Reviewed PR #2340 (https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2340), head `64e803df`, one commit on base `ea352306`. Main has since moved one commit, to `50e17b36` (LIN-4331 close-out F1/F2: a README row edit and a paragraph added to the paper about facts at the pin). The PR is still MERGEABLE, and nothing in that paragraph contradicts the essay. It confirms the comment-cap fix and the empty `PRESENCE_ALLOW` the essay cites.

CI: green on `64e803df`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and CI success all passed (run 42249846956).

**Scope against plan.** The PR changes 8 files: the essay, three SVGs, `charts.mjs`, the README row, one `proposals.md` line, and the library essay-count pin (13 → 14). That matches the plan's scope. The test pin is the only file the plan didn't name, and it's a direct consequence of adding one essay. The prequel wasn't touched, and no shared SVG helper was added.

**What I checked myself**
- **Numbers.** I checked every load-bearing number in the essay against v2 `@ea352306`, its evidence folder, or the Periodical it cites. All of these are found there: 17/3/1/0; +0.38, +0.39, +0.50, +0.37; 8 and 19; 22 of 68 and 29 of 68; $8.16; the three cost pairs and 47/65/85%; 143 comments; the catch-all going 16 → 17; "seven merges", with the paper's list at `:112`; LIN-4252's 17 copies; and "four ordinary pairs … from one day (20 October)" at `:99`. The census values 56 → 25 (9 stops) at `af55cb73`, 10 at `5c63aa26`, and 6 at `ce42e7217` come straight from `git/census-by-merge.json`, and so does the essay's "25 to 10 over the Drift window". The crude grep 46 → 51 is at `drift-coherence…@509f797e:238`. "About fifty" guards matches Seams run 9 `:13,152`: "50 of 51 deleted lines, by crude token match".
- **Wording constraints.** The essay uses v2's exact phrase "nine area readings over fifteen tickets, all better in both passes, and no pass read one worse". It contains no "7 of 7" or "seven areas". The baseline appears as "one of four" with the consolidation line and the explicit "not loop against no loop", in both the text and the Figure 2 caption. LIN-4312, LIN-4322 and `afe9074f` are stated as facts at commits, with no verdict words. The person's-seat cases are not attributed to John. The Hanoi recursion is marked as Claude's gloss.
- **Code citations.** I re-read each one with `git show ea352306:<path>`. `fetchIssueComments` throws when the comments can't be read whole (`lib/providers/linear/index.js:1169-1182`). `declaresPeriodicalGrant` is at `lib/dispatch-entrance.js:1218`. `PRESENCE_ALLOW = {}` is at `:181`. All six census entries are `// stop:` at `fake-dom-census.test.js:53-58`.
- **Figures.** I re-ran `charts.mjs` into the committed figure folder, then ran `node scripts/figure-theme.mjs`. The worktree stayed byte-identical, so the figures really are generated by the script. `--check` passes. The script reads `2026-11-06-v2/` in place by a path relative to itself and copies no data. Before `591bb9596` the census figure draws only the total, as the plan requires.
- **Mutation checks (LIN-2274), all reverted afterwards:**
  - I removed the essay file. `library.test.js` went red ("the excerpt rule…" failed), so the 14-essay pin is load-bearing.
  - I pointed `charts.mjs` at v1's evidence folder (`2026-11-06/`). It failed with `AssertionError: nine area readings`, so the script's assertions really do guard what it plots.
- **Tests.** `node --test tests/unit/library.test.js tests/unit/library-security.test.js` passed 54/54 on the PR head. I didn't re-run the full unit suite, because CI covers it.
- **Regressions.** Every content file is new. The README, `proposals.md` and test edits each add one line, or change one, and nothing was reverted or overwritten.
- **Registries.** The README row has two sentences and no version history. The `proposals.md` line is new and says what it's for, and lines `:663-665` are untouched. That meets standard.md rule 3 / `:83`, which asks for at least one line.

**Isolated or one of a class?** Isolated. This is one new document. The plan already handled the parallel claim surfaces: the notebook's stale "7" and "two days" are frozen history the essay doesn't take numbers from, and the one live registry, the README, uses v2's wording.

**Fixes for close-out to make (small, text only)**
1. Essay reading list item 12 (`the-place-became-somebodys-job.md:131`) cites the blind-read prompt with no sha. Change the path to `docs/papers/harbour/cleaner-than-it-started-evidence/2026-11-06/prompts/blind-read-prompt.md@ea352306`. I checked that the file exists at that commit. Also add the same entry to the front-matter `sources` array, because the essay leans on that prompt for its main limit.
2. The PR description has escaped backticks (`\``) that render literally. This is cosmetic: fix it with `gh pr edit 2340 --body-file` when close-out merges.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **The essay and its three figures render correctly in the Library, in light and dark themes.** *Inside* this ticket's done-when ("figures … labelled so a fresh reader can follow them"). CI parses the catalog and `figure-theme --check` checks the theming markup, but no one looked at the rendered page. Settle **before the merge**: open `/library/harbour/the-place-became-somebodys-job` on a local server at head `64e803df` (or later) and confirm the following:
  - all three SVGs load (no broken image);
  - in dark theme, the Figure 2 cells and the Figure 3 legend are readable;
  - Figure 3's "6 · 6 Nov 11:41Z" label doesn't collide with the line.
- **The fresh-reader step was done by models, not people.** *Inside* (done-when: "two fresh readers"). The ticket asked for fresh readers, and the essay's `model:` line records both subagents (Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5). It also says "not independently checked by a person", which is honest. My numeral check above covers what an accuracy reader would cover. Nothing to settle beyond confirming that this disclosure stays in the merged text.
- **The merge onto current main (`50e17b36`).** *Inside*, because the essay cites v2 and v2 changed after the base. I checked it: the new paragraph agrees with the essay, and GitHub reports the PR as mergeable. Close-out re-checks CI on the exact merge commit as usual. **Discharged**, apart from that routine re-check.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger: the rendered-page check before the merge, plus the two small text fixes above. The essay meets the ticket and the scope call. Every number I checked traces to v2, its evidence folder or the cited reports. The figures are generated and their assertions hold under mutation.

Correction to the review above: close-out fix 1 (the blind-read prompt citation with no sha) is at `docs/papers/harbour/the-place-became-somebodys-job.md:143`, not `:131`. The fix itself is unchanged.

## Close-out — LIN-4330

**Merged:** PR #2340 (https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2340), squash-merged as `b76d5239` on main, pinned with `--match-head-commit 687eb126` (the commit CI passed on). Review verdict on record: Approve, conditional on the ledger below.

**Changes I made after the approval** (commit `687eb126`; nobody reviewed these, so each is listed against what prompted it):
1. **Review fix 1** (the blind-read prompt cited with no sha, essay line 143): reading-list item 12 now cites `…/2026-11-06/prompts/blind-read-prompt.md@ea352306`, and the same path is added to front-matter `sources`. I confirmed the file exists at that commit.
2. **Review fix 2** (escaped backticks in the PR description): fixed with `gh pr edit 2340 --body-file`, and a close-out section added to the body.
3. **Found while settling the rendered-page item:** Figure 1 (the loop) had reversed arrowheads between the columns, the "After the merge" text clipped at the box edge, and its dashed-arrow label struck through by the arrow. Fixed in `the-place-became-somebodys-job-scripts/charts.mjs` (columns narrowed to leave room for forward arrows, the box text wrapped to two lines, the label moved below the curve). Only `loop-before-during-after.svg` was regenerated; Figures 2 and 3 are byte-identical. `node scripts/figure-theme.mjs --check` passes. No wording, number or claim changed.

**Ledger:**
- *Rendered page, light and dark (inside, before merge):* done. I served the PR head locally, screenshotted all three figures in both themes, and all three SVGs loaded. Figure 3 (the census) has its "6 · 6 Nov 11:41Z" label clear of the line, in dark as well as light. The area-readings figure's cells and legend are readable in dark. Figure 1's three defects, above, were the thing this check found. I re-checked the same page after the fix.
- *Fresh readers were models (inside):* the disclosure stays in the merged text (`model:` line: "not independently checked by a person"). Nothing else to settle.
- *Merge onto current main `50e17b36` (inside):* the review had read it as compatible; GitHub reported MERGEABLE and the merge was clean; CI re-run on the exact head (below).
- *Outside items:* none recorded by review, so nothing to file. No related tickets to close (no relations or children on this ticket).
- *Named monitor/rollback:* none was named, none is claimed. This is a docs-only change.

**CI on the final head `687eb126`** (run 42252238936): Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success all SUCCESS. Also `node --test tests/unit/library.test.js tests/unit/library-security.test.js`: 54 pass, 0 fail, locally.

**After the deploy:** production's footer moved from `50e17b36` to `b76d5239`. On https://harbour.cat/library/the-place-became-somebodys-job: HTTP 200; all three figure URLs return 200 and render in light and dark; the live loop SVG contains the fixed text; the live page contains the `@ea352306` citation.

**Not run:** nothing outstanding.

**Description:** archived first (snapshot `2026-11-06T16:22:49Z` verified to hold the full 22,360-character pre-prune description), then the Implementation Plan body replaced by a stub. Problem statement, argument, material, done-when and the scope-call section are kept.
